e: Authorities pledge about $2 million for humanitarian aid in Yemen.
A Cirrus SR22 light aircraft crashes into a mountain slope near Leukerbad, killing three people.
A 200-page dossier on Nazi war criminal Josef Mengele, nicknamed the "Angel of Death," is published by the Federal Intelligence Service.
Five people die when a tourist coach crashes in Grisons.
A hydroelectric plant explosion kills two people in Piotta.
A woman is killed and five people are wounded, one critically in a rave shooting in Aarau.
The United States imposes a 12.5% tariff on Switzerland, citing the presence of alleged forced labour in the supply chain.
Three people are injured in a stabbing attack at Winterthur railway station.
Switzerland halts weapons exports to the United States, citing its principle of neutrality and US involvement in the 2026 Iran war.
One person is killed when a cable car cabin crashes down a snowy mountainside in Engelberg, Obwalden.
At least six people are killed in an arson attack on a postal bus in Kerzers.
A train is derailed by an avalanche near Goppenstein, injuring five people.

Sanija Ameti, a member of the Zurich municipal council, is fined CHF3,500 for publishing images of herself firing a pistol at an auction poster of a 14th-century painting of the Madonna and Child by Tommaso del Mazza in 2024.
The federal government imposes a four-year freeze on any assets held by Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his close associates in Switzerland.
At least 41 people are killed in a fire at a bar in Crans-Montana, Valais.
